name: bm25_hybrid
summary: Add lexical BM25 retrieval alongside the existing pure-vector search inside HotelKnowledgeRetriever.document_search() and fuse the two ranked lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF, k=60). BM25 catches exact-keyword matches (e.g. "WiFi password") that the dense embedder under-ranks, while the dense vector continues to handle paraphrase / Thai-English cross-lingual queries. Picking Option B2 (local rank_bm25) over B1 (Qdrant-native hybrid) because (a) rank_bm25==0.2.2 is already installed but fastembed (needed for Qdrant sparse vectors) is not, and (b) the existing collection was created with a single unnamed dense vector — attaching a sparse named vector to it would require dropping and re-creating the collection plus a full re-ingest of all 49 chunks. B2 is a pure code change scoped to one method; no schema migration, no re-ingest, no new dependency.
root_cause: Pure dense vector retrieval (qwen3-embedding-8b → Qdrant) is a semantic-similarity match and systematically under-weights rare literal tokens. Q1 "what is the WiFi password" is the canonical failure: the chunk containing the literal string "WiFi password: HOTEL2024GUEST" does not rise to rank #1 because semantically many hotel-amenity chunks ("WiFi available throughout property", "internet access", "guest services") score similarly under cosine similarity. BM25's IDF term makes the rare bigram "WiFi password" heavily discriminative, so it ranks that one exact-match chunk first. RRF (1/(60+r)) fuses the two rankings without needing to calibrate score scales between BM25 (unbounded) and cosine (0..1), and is the de-facto standard for hybrid lexical+dense fusion (Cormack et al. 2009; used by Elasticsearch, Vespa, Qdrant native hybrid).

files_touched.location_hint: Add module-level _bm25_index cache + _build_bm25_index() helper after the CONFIG block (~line 133). Modify HotelKnowledgeRetriever.document_search() (lines 301-436) to (a) run vector search as today, (b) run BM25 search over the same corpus, (c) fuse via RRF, (d) return top num_docs. Add a HYBRID_ENABLED env flag (default true) so it can be disabled for A/B comparison in eval.
files_touched.rationale: Self-contained code change. Lazy-builds an in-memory BM25Okapi once per worker (49 chunks → trivial memory), runs both retrievals on every query, fuses with RRF k=60 (industry default). Env flags HYBRID_RETRIEVAL=false, RRF_K, BM25_TOP_K let the thesis A/B compare cleanly in scripts/eval/run_evaluation.py.

files_touched.location_hint: Invalidate the BM25 cache at the end of ingest_docs() (~line 267), ingest_text() (~line 295), delete_documents() (~line 506), and clear_collection() (~line 528).
files_touched.exact_diff_or_content:
# After each successful mutation:
_bm25_state["index"] = None
_bm25_state["docs"] = None

logger.info("BM25 index invalidated (will rebuild on next search)")
files_touched.rationale: BM25 index is a stale cache once chunks are added or removed. Invalidating triggers a one-shot rebuild on the next query, which for 49 chunks is <50ms.

live_smoke_test.question: Does Q1 'what is the WiFi password' now return the chunk containing the literal 'WiFi password: HOTEL2024GUEST' at rank #1, and does Q2 'breakfast time' still return the 6:30 AM - 10:30 AM breakfast chunk in the top-3 (no regression)?
live_smoke_test.before_signature: With pure vector retrieval, Q1 returns the WiFi-credentials chunk at rank 3-5 (or absent from top-3) — primary_assistant frequently answers 'please contact reception' instead of revealing the password directly. Q2 already returns the breakfast chunk at rank 1.
live_smoke_test.after_pass_criteria: POST /chat 'what is the WiFi password' → response contains the literal password token (e.g. HOTEL2024GUEST, or whichever value is in data/hotel/*.md). Inspect server logs: 'Returning N hybrid (RRF) results' line is present, and the WiFi chunk appears at rank 1 with a fused RRF score >= ~0.032 (i.e. 1/60 + 1/60). POST /chat 'breakfast time' → response still cites the 6:30 AM - 10:30 AM window; the breakfast chunk appears in top-3 of hybrid results. Run scripts/eval/run_evaluation.py with HYBRID_RETRIEVAL=true vs HYBRID_RETRIEVAL=false: retrieval recall@5 for the WiFi question goes from 0 → 1; aggregate recall@5 across the eval set does not drop.
